coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing found: no register, licence or reporting duty for households as employers surfaced in the labour-migration search; the sector appears informal. Nothing new beyond K02 for the agency side.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Licence exists: 'preparation, processing and distribution of ferrous and non-ferrous metal scrap and waste' (item 12, industry ministry) in the annex to the Law on the Permit System (2023, amended 2024). Licences are open-ended, so no renewal cycle. No purchase-register rule or software found. Recycling is mostly artisanal (24 small firms, per Current Time).

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnshops are licensed (item 9 in the financial-sector block of the permit law annex; fee 500 base units) and, per the Nacbank pawnshop regulation of 2000 as described by a legal database, lend only against property of Tajik citizens. Reporting duties to the National Bank not confirmed. No licence regime found for general second-hand dealers.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Licence for buying precious metals, jewellery and scrap from the public (item 4, finance ministry); separate certificate for jewellery manufacture and assay/certification of precious metals and stones. The 2003 hallmarking resolution is shown as no longer in force, so the current hallmark regime is unverified. Purchase-register or reporting duties not confirmed.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler licence found. A permit list item exists for converting vehicles and their parts (internal affairs permits, wording partly truncated). Import restrictions on old cars (pre-2013, from 1 Jan 2024 per Kazakh press) and a reported sharp utilisation-fee rise (Current Time, undated) are unverified. Nothing usable as a recurring small-business duty.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Vet-service stations issue vet certificates, pre-slaughter certificates, and handle registration, branding and clinical exam of animals (2015 paid-services list). Vet-sanitary expertise is required for meat sold in markets. No electronic animal ID or traceability system found for Tajikistan (Kyrgyzstan has one).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Vet-sanitary expertise of meat at markets by laboratories; sale outside designated places or without expertise is banned (2009 procedure). No slaughterhouse licence or butcher register found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Law on Beekeeping (2003, amended 2008): activity needs no licence. About 270,000 colonies and 4,620 t honey (MIR 24, undated). No apiary register or honey export certificate rule found. Not a compliance market.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Licence for 'private veterinary activities' including selling veterinary medicines and biologicals (item 46, food-safety body, open-ended). Selling vet drugs needs a licence; products need Central State Vet Drug Control Centre certification. No e-register of vet drug movements found (Kyrgyzstan has one).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Permit for special use of water and drilling of water wells (permit item 25, environment body), issued for an unlimited period. Water Law covers special water use. No licensing register or digital process found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Licence for collecting, storing and transporting hazardous waste (item 42); permit to set waste generation rates (permit item 27). No general sanitation or septic licence found. Municipal garbage collection details not found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Industrial Safety Law No 14 of 2004 exists; permit annex lists a 'certificate of registration of hazardous production facilities' (work-safety body). No specific lift, boiler or pressure-vessel inspection rules or private inspectors found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Rural drinking water is a large gap (about half the population lacks safe water; vendors and cisterns used). Water user associations under the 2006 law are irrigation-focused. No compliance reporting duty for small drinking-water systems found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Law on Safe Handling of Pesticides and Agrochemicals (2003, amended 2007, 2012) requires permits from the authorised body for sale, storage, transport and import after registration tests; plant quarantine law of 2019 and state catalogue. No separate dealer licence in the licence annex. New Law on Organic Production of 19 Dec 2024 not relevant to dealers.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Licence for employing Tajik citizens abroad and foreign citizens in Tajikistan (item 33, new Ministry of Labour, Migration and Employment set up by Resolution 117 of 28 Feb 2025). Moscow Times (26 May 2026, snippet only) reports Russia approved organised recruitment from Tajikistan with fingerprinting, photo and medical checks in Dushanbe before departure; this is a possible new trigger for K02.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Nothing usable: law on regulating traditions and ceremonies bans slaughter and feasts at funerals; headstone size standards and cemetery inspections by the Committee for Religious Affairs. No burial register or funeral licence found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Ministry of Justice register shows about 1,545 public associations and 51 trade unions (undated study). Foreign-funding notification within 10 days per ICNL guide (undated). No recurring annual-report form confirmed; halal supervision nothing found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Road passenger and cargo transport licence (item 35, transport body; domestic and international passenger, freight, freight forwarding), open-ended; vehicle maintenance and repair licence (item 37). Patent rules also make transport organisations report contracted entrepreneurs to tax quarterly. No GPS or tachograph rule found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Government Resolution 151 of 31 Mar 2022 (in force) para 11: market and shopping-centre administrations must e-report to the tax office by the 10th after each quarter on traders, trading rows, area, vehicles and fees collected. Money changers: NBT closed all exchange points in Nov 2015 (bank-only); 'foreign exchange' remains a listed licensed activity (item 78), current status of non-bank exchangers unverified.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Searches for driving schools and private kindergartens returned only unrelated countries; education licensing not located in the permit annex extract. Hunting and fauna use needs permits (permit item 26). Food production and sale needs licence under food-safety body (item 46 third bullet). Nothing confirmed as a recurring small-premises duty.

result.competitor: None found. Searches in Russian and Tajik turned up no software, service or Tax Committee e-service for this report. I couldn't verify whether the Tax Committee's free cabinet takes the upload or what format is required, so a free state channel may exist (unverifiable). Excel is the obvious substitute.
result.duty: Resolution No. 151 of 31.03.2022 (registered with the Ministry of Justice 06.04.2022, No. 191, status in force), paragraph 11. Market administrations, trade centres and transport organisations must send quarterly electronic information to the tax office where they are registered, by the 10th of the month after the quarter. It covers the number of entrepreneurs, location including trading rows and area, vehicles, and service or rent fees. No specific penalty is set: paragraph 47 refers to general liability under Tajik law. I couldn't find the matching Tax Code 2021 (No. 1844) article or administrative fine (searched, not found). The duty originated in Resolution No. 45 of 25.01.2017, which amended Resolution No. 451 of 2012; No. 451 was repealed by No. 151.
result.market: Not found. stat.tj gave no count of markets or trade centres, and a WFP survey from 2011 covered about 30 food markets. My rough estimate is a few hundred markets and trade centres plus some transport organisations (unverified).
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Paragraph 11 of Government Resolution No. 151 of 31.03.2022 (spinform marks it "Действует"; no later amendments listed) requires administrations of markets and trade centres, and transport organisations, to send the local tax office electronic information each quarter by the 10th of the following month. The information covers the entrepreneurs they host, their trading rows and area, vehicles, and the fees or rent they charge. No specific fine is named: paragraph 47 only refers to general liability. I found no commercial tool for this report, but I also couldn't confirm the format or the Tax Committee portal. The job is simple and could be done in Excel. There are probably only hundreds of operators (number not found). Low pain and weak enforcement mean low willingness to pay.

result.competitor: I found no Tajik commercial software for premix dosing logs or fortification compliance. Adjacent tools: FortifyMIS, an online fortification-monitoring system from Project Healthy Children and GAIN that is donor-funded and free to the user (used in Mozambique, no Tajik deployment found). WFP also gives Tajik mills free training and lab supplies (10 mills in April 2026), and donor-backed digital tools could be adopted at no cost. The core control is hardware (micro-feeders/dosers) plus lab testing, not software.
result.duty: Real and in force. Government Resolution No. 508 of 27 Jul 2026 (Spinform lists it as "in force") requires that, from 1 Sep 2026, higher- and first-grade wheat flour sold domestically be fortified with iron, zinc, B9 and B12. Unfortified flour of these grades is allowed only for export under contract. The Ministry of Health does the sanitary-hygienic control and the Ministry of Industry keeps "constant supervision" of mills. The Ministry of Industry, not the mills, files the analytical reports, and the visible text sets no frequency. In the visible text, mills have no record-keeping, reporting or inspection-frequency duty, and no penalties are stated; the rest of the text is paywalled. The 2020 MoH sanitary rules (reg. no. 1028) set the nutrient levels, but I could not read the FAOLEX PDF. A UN document mentions a plan to issue 'Permission to Work' certificates to new mills only if they have micro-feeders, premix stock and written fortification procedures. The 2019 law had weak enforcement.
result.market: Very small and concentrated. The Food Fortification Initiative (2020) says 18 large and medium mills control about 90% of milling output, and an earlier WFP assessment says 6 plants make about 60%. The total count of small mills is not found. Q1 2026 output of 219,251 t comes from a secondary search snippet. Domestic production covers about 40% of demand; the rest is imported flour or grain from Kazakhstan.
result.reason: The duty exists (Resolution 508, in force from 1 Sep 2026), and I found no local software doing the job, so the claim holds. But mills have no stated record-keeping or reporting duty and no published penalties. About 18 mills make roughly 90% of output, so few buyers exist, and small mills in Tajikistan likely won't pay much. Donors (WFP, GAIN) give free training and lab kits, and FortifyMIS-type tools could arrive free. The real compliance problem is hardware (micro-feeders) and premix supply, not logging. The 2019 law went largely unenforced. Distribution would be easy through donor channels, but revenue potential is tiny.
